in writing. - the illegal trade in electronic waste is booming. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal. in germany alone, around 700 000 tonnes of e-waste were generated in 2010. 155 000 tonnes of it is illegally shipped to countries like ghana every year. either waste pickers, who have already been paid by the equipment manufacturers for recycling, are handing the scrap to retailers, or citizens are being stopped at the gates of the municipal recycling yards and the equipment is bought off for a few euros. the new e-waste directive is intended to provide the authorities with a legally binding basis for defining clearly what constitutes waste and what constitutes a second-hand product. when refrigerators or mobile phones are discontinued, expensive raw materials such as gold, copper or silver are to be reused in europe. in addition, proper recycling reduces the poisoning of people and the environment by e-waste. the aim of the directive is a noble one, and it remains to be seen what effect it will have in practice. if dealers are not allowed to take back used equipment, it is feared that a lot of electrical waste will be dumped illegally. that is why i voted against it.

in writing. − biocides are active substances and preparations containing one or more active substances, in the form in which they reach the user, which are intended to destroy, deter, render harmless, prevent harm from harmful organisms or otherwise combat them by chemical or biological means. the relevant eu directive explains this definition in detail. biocidal products are used in a wide range of sectors and applications, such as wood preservatives. the eu biocidal products directive therefore distinguishes 23 product types into four main groups (disinfectants and general biocidal products; means of protection; pesticides; or other biocidal products). biocidal products will be subject to a national authorisation/registration procedure in each eu member state from 2009 onwards, based on an official evaluation of their efficacy and their risks to humans, animals and the environment. this is to avoid inadequate efficacy and unacceptable effects when used properly. a biocidal product authorisation shall also include mandatory labelling particulars and, where appropriate, conditions of use. in the report i voted in favour of the amendments to the original draft, as i consider it important that the active substances which are subject to a simplified authorisation procedure are now listed in the annex to the regulation.
in writing. − a central community authorisation system for biocidal products is an important step towards a harmonised european market in this field. it is the most efficient solution to improve the availability of these products, to stimulate innovation and to ensure effective protection of human health and the environment. a central community authorisation further guarantees consistent assessments and uniform requirements in all member states, leading to a higher level of consumer protection.

in writing. − the eu's sanctions policy against authoritarian regimes is only credible if member states speak with one voice and there are clear criteria as to when restrictive measures such as asset freezes are necessary. authoritarian leaders and their partners must not be allowed to own property, invest money or train in european institutions within the eu. i therefore agreed.
in writing. − the crossborder transfer of a company's registered office from one member state to another is associated with bureaucratic red tape, legal uncertainty and costs. of course, there are also social effects which the workers feel. although the court of justice has concluded that better harmonisation of the rules is necessary, this is still a matter for the legislator. finally, the aim is to prevent the abuse of letterbox companies and shell companies to circumvent legal, social and tax conditions. the court of justice in particular has not necessarily taken the side of the workers in this context in the past, most recently in its judgment on chain contracts. i cannot therefore agree to the proposed amendments.
in writing. − a directive on the transnational transfer of the seat of a company is essential if the freedom of establishment, as one of the fundamental pillars of the internal market, is to be able to have its full effect. european companies should be able to move their headquarters to another member state without the need for prior liquidation. at the same time, the relocation of the company's headquarters must ensure that labour standards and the principles of employee participation are maintained.
in writing. − together, the european commission and the member states of the european union make up the world's largest community of humanitarian aid providers, year after year. this amount amounted to eur 2957 million in 2010, of which about one third was used under the european commission's grant. the european commission's echo directorate-general is responsible for implementing the union's aid policy, which is delivered to those in need through 200 partner organisations, un specialised agencies and ngos. it is of the utmost importance that the use of community funds allocated to assistance is properly monitored by the competent bodies of the union, in which the european parliament has a key role. i fully support the report unanimously adopted by the committee on budgetary control in which the rapporteur summarises the operation, effectiveness and results of the community's aid policy in the specific crises in pakistan and haiti.
in writing. − to illustrate the importance of humanitarian aid in the eu budget, it is worth mentioning that in 2010 €1.115 billion was allocated to it. the european commission's echo directorate-general manages the aid and is responsible for the management of the money. an important instrument for providing assistance is the conclusion of contracts with ngos. unfortunately, in the past, the kotrol mechanisms have been heavily criticized because tasks in this area are delegated to international organizations, each of which is subject only to its own control systems. the amendments in this report make the control system more transparent, more comprehensive and more general, which is why i have given my approval to this report.
in writing. − with a total of eur 2 957 million (in 2010), the eu is the world's largest donor of development aid. this total contribution is made up of contributions from the member states (64%) and the commission (36%). echo is the directorate-general (dg) responsible for the implementation of humanitarian aid and disaster response by the eu. dg echo operates internationally by supporting some 200 partners ngos, un agencies, international organisations worldwide. the actions are managed from the commission's headquarters in brussels through a network of more than 40 offices in all the areas of operation. the problem is that budget implementation and budgetary control in these areas is not centrally carried out by the commission, but is outsourced to various international organizations which carry it out in accordance with their own procedures of accounting, auditing and internal control. in accordance with the principle of the sole examination, the commission does not carry out any additional examinations. it shall confine itself to carrying out on-the-spot monitoring and verification visits. the european court of auditors has repeatedly criticised this delegation of administration for leading to a lack of coherence, a complex web of legislation and insufficient control and follow-up of the use of eu funds. i can therefore only welcome the commission's approach to this problem in the revision of the financial regulation.
in writing. − improving and making more transparent the allocation of funds under the echo programme is essential to ensure the efficient and economic use of eu budget funds. this is necessary in particular to avoid double financing. in selecting local ngo partners, cost-effectiveness must be considered alongside their expertise and past successes. humanitarian aid needs to be made more sustainable by focusing more on disaster prevention.

in writing. − the linking of business registers is a welcome step, as it aims to create a platform that can improve and accelerate communication and information retrieval for citizens and businesses. this will promote the integration of the economic area within the eu and strengthen legal certainty for businesses and citizens. but trade registers differ in many ways across the eu member states, for example in terms of their legal significance and the reliability of the data they collect. it is clear that the increasing cross-border economic activity requires better interconnection of business registers for reasons of legal certainty and transparency. the aim of the directive is merely to link existing national registers in a purely technical way and not to harmonise the legal effects. the exchange of register information is the only regulation and no trade register is established with its own data. i believe that the linking of business registers can only succeed if the commission and the member states work together even more closely. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. questions - and solutions - must emerge as the network is built and then be developed. there are still many open questions to be answered, which is why i abstained.
in writing. − the increase in crossborder economic activity resulting from the increasing integration of the european internal market makes it imperative to link national business registers. in addition to improving transparency and legal certainty, such a measure also saves time and money. only through a europe-wide link can electronic business registers reach their full potential.
in writing. − fisheries agreements are a fixed point of the common fisheries policy and are designed to give the eu's fishing fleet a greater weight over the fleets of other fishing nations and to continue to grant them access to exploitable fishery resources under the jurisdiction of other states (after the extension of the exclusive economic zone from 12 to 200 nautical miles in the 1970s). these agreements thus have an impact on the fishing activities of the eu fleet in international waters and in waters of third countries. i have voted in favour of the report because there seems to be no objection to it.
in writing. − the eu's fishing industry is the third largest in the world and eu fisheries policy is a common concern with the 27 member states. the eu's common fisheries policy is based on free and equal access to fish stocks in eu waters, international waters and waters of third countries with which the eu has agreements. the eu's main motives for concluding fisheries agreements with third countries are to meet their growing demand for fish, to preserve jobs in the fishing industry, to exploit the 40% overcapacity of the eu fleet and to protect stocks in its own waters. the eu and guinea-bissau have now decided to strengthen cooperation between fisheries operators. this is welcome, and that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. − the eu-guinea-bissau fisheries agreement brings wide-ranging benefits to both parties: the eu is opening up additional fishing opportunities, and guinea-bissau is benefiting from eu financial contributions and improved standards of hygiene, as well as from the fight against illegal fishing. the new protocol is particularly welcome because it allows the eu to suspend financial payments if human rights or democratic standards are not respected in guinea-bissau.
in writing. - the gradual approximation of morocco to the european internal market and morocco's participation in community programmes will significantly improve bilateral relations between the two parties. the protocol is intended to support morocco in implementing economic, political and social reforms in the interest of the citizens. at the same time, it will ensure that all areas of morocco, including western sahara, benefit from the eu's financial assistance.
in writing. − bluetongue is a painful disease in ruminants and has caused considerable economic damage since the first outbreaks in 2000. third countries stopped their imports from some eu countries altogether despite vaccination of breeding animals. the problem of cattle breeding is, in any case, an existential one and it needs solutions. the old directive on bluetongue dates back to 2000, when there was no good vaccine. today, vaccines are more mature and without serious side effects, so it is good that the old directive is being adapted.
in writing. − mass vaccination against bluetongue can help reduce clinical illness and losses, contain the spread of the disease and facilitate safe trade in live animals. given the different risk of disease, which varies by region, the cost of mandatory vaccination is questionable. the risk of disease appears to be higher in the southern and western regions of the eu than in the northern and eastern regions. in addition, morbidity and mortality are dependent on several factors. i have therefore abstained.
in writing. − bluetongue is a viral infection in ruminants which, in the worst case, leads to the death of the animals. the disease is notifiable as an animal disease and is not transmissible to humans and is not dangerous. it has been found that the enormous damage in vaccinated animals is immediately apparent after vaccination. among the symptoms of vaccinated animals are decreased milk production, and worse still, stillbirths, diarrhoea, and generally poor health. in goats, the young died after drinking the milk of the freshly vaccinated mother. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat the spread of the disease. if they do not avoid all meat and dairy products, you would certainly be "enjoying" the poisons of the bluetongue vaccine. i am also informed by experts that there is a concern that this vaccine may not be able to identify the real pathogens. the question of whether the animals treated in this way still have 'organic quality' and the impact of vaccination on the quality of meat and on the healthy development of future generations are all legitimate questions which i believe are still unresolved. for these reasons i have abstained.
in writing. − technical progress and the single european payment area have advantages. for example, better liquidity planning through sepa info on the exact day of the account being debited or shorter transfer times or when debit cards can be used not only at atms to withdraw cash but also to pay throughout europe. however, iban and bic are more complicated and not as common to many people, especially the elderly. it is therefore welcome that parliament has taken the initiative to ensure that old direct debit orders remain valid. in particular, in the face of the massive increase in cybercrime, where allegedly free online offers that turn out to be expensive, or hacker attacks and the spying on personal user data - especially bank data - cause major financial damage, it is all the more important that the unconditional right of withdrawal for withdrawals remains in place. the transition periods are too short and it would be desirable for the elderly in particular to maintain the old systems in parallel with sepa. i therefore abstained.

in writing. − the current financial and sovereign debt crisis can only be countered by reforming the general economic environment and by medium- and long-term growth-enhancing measures. full implementation of the eu guidelines for the implementation of strategy 2020 and strengthening of banks' capital adequacy are needed to restore investor confidence. the public administration must also be made more transparent and efficient and legal certainty must be guaranteed in the rules on services of general economic interest. the social consequences of the crisis must also be adequately addressed by adopting structural reforms for labour markets and investing in growth-enhancing areas such as education and research.

in writing. − to reduce the risk of a 'bank run' and to avoid the taxpayer being called upon to pay for the failure of credit institutions in future crises, it is essential to create uniform minimum standards for deposit protection across europe. all credit institutions without exception should be required to be members of a deposit guarantee scheme and all deposit guarantee schemes must be adequately financed ex ante. in addition, short withdrawal periods in the event of compensation should be used to strengthen the confidence of depositors. i think it would be appropriate to introduce a european-wide refund period of five working days instead of the current twenty working days.
in writing. − the debt and economic crisis and the sometimes harsh national austerity policies adopted or to be adopted by many eu member states make it all the more important that the european union too should take austerity measures. although there were no breakthroughs on the big issues such as the three seats in parliament or the subsidy and agency jungle, the report made it clear that savings were needed. the report gives only half-hearted guidelines, although these are of course better than nothing. i voted in that direction.
in writing. - in these economically difficult times for the member states, the realistic approach to saving advocated by mr vaughan is correct and deserves our support. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. and we can certainly achieve further savings if we improve interinstitutional cooperation and cooperate better in areas such as staff, organisation or building management. however, while savings are necessary, there are also areas where caution is required: firstly, environmental protection, because we need an efficient environmental policy in all eu institutions and bodies. the institutions themselves should be the model for europe. secondly, in the area of translation and language services, where savings were made last year. but this cannot go on like this. the european parliament is the legislator for 500 million europeans. and these citizens must be able to understand our work in their own language. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council.
in writing. - in times of increasing overfishing of stocks, there should be more discussion about the introduction of fishing quotas and, consequently, about how to comply with and control them. however, science has not yet been able to pinpoint the exact number of fish, in this case the stocks of the cod. consequently, all measures are based on estimates only. nevertheless, they should be used to establish a tac. i have voted in favour of the resolution because in the long term it will be necessary to maintain or restore fish stocks at a level which will ensure the highest possible yield.

in writing. - hungary has a new democratically elected government which, like any government, is enacting new laws. the argument is now that this restricts fundamental freedoms and that the eu is therefore concerned about the situation of the hungarian population. of course, there must be no violation of fundamental rights in an eu member state. the high degree of fundamental rights and freedoms must in any case be maintained and upheld. in the case of the criticism of hungary, however, the question arises whether other motivations are not at the forefront. hungary has elected a 'right-wing' government, which seems to be a thorn in the side of the 'left-wing' governments of other member states and the politically correct good people here in the eu parliament. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. in austria and other eu countries, the central bank and the constitutional court are also de facto politically occupied. the european union has a long history of human rights violations, and it is not easy to find a solution to these problems. but that is precisely why fundamental rights should not be used as a pretext, otherwise they may one day turn out to be just more empty words. i therefore voted against the resolution.
in writing. the eu is seeking to set a precedent ahead of the russian parliamentary elections. she's complaining about long-standing grievances, hoping to influence the upcoming election. the eu is angry that russia has twice voted against intervention in syria at the un security council, which is why the eu now wants to play the role of teacher but does not start turning around on its own doorstep. unfortunately, not all member states have the same level of fundamental freedoms as some eu countries. but the eu should first improve its own acquis before it harasses other countries. in some countries, for example, freedom of expression is de facto only partially guaranteed or is increasingly restricted by new laws, such as the new, ineffective law against incitement in austria. the resolution's recitals state that enhanced cooperation and improved relations with russia bring more stability, prosperity and security. the motion for a resolution is the exact opposite. russia is an independent country and that must be respected more. i cannot therefore agree to this request.

in writing. - there is no justification for extending the fisheries agreement. the extension of the fisheries agreement with morocco, which is considered to be environmentally harmful and which, at some 36 million euros a year, is not only one of the most expensive agreements (and which does not benefit either the european taxpayer or the local population), must be categorically rejected. the agreement is interpreted by both parties to include the rich fishing grounds of the occupied western sahara, which are now threatened by overfishing. this is contrary to the un convention on the law of the sea and international law. the eu's illegal and legalized plundering of the sea off the occupied western sahara must come to an end.
in writing. − the draft agreement will allow morocco to immediately liberalise 45% of the value of imports from the european union while the community will liberalise 55% of its imports from morocco. the agreement also provides for increased concessions in the fruit and vegetable sector, in which moroccan products account for 80% of the eu’s imports. this agreement should not go into effect without fulfilling import control mechanisms as pointed out by olaf because it does not benefit small farmers in morocco (over 70% of exports are in the hands of three firms), it includes the disputed saharan territories (the un does not recognise the sovereignty of morocco) and it would mean the progressive disappearance and marginalisation of a number of european agricultural products.

in writing. − in many european countries, blind and visually impaired people are still not included in statistics, so there can only be rough estimates of their numbers. in denmark, finland, the united kingdom, ireland, iceland, italy and the netherlands, blind and partially sighted persons are counted. the world health organization (who) evaluated surveys from these countries. this has shown that the number of visually impaired people in these countries has increased by 80%. similar developments are expected for the rest of the eu member states. the reason is thought to be an ageing population. it is therefore all the more important to ensure that visually impaired people have greater access to literature, for example, without barriers. to date, only 5% of all printed works published in the eu are in braille, large-print or audio recordings. i have voted in favour of the resolution because it is essential for the further education of the population that printed matter should also be made available to visually impaired people.

in writing. - the present report, which calls for an increase in the participation of women in decision-making processes, is unfortunately a complete failure. instead of analysing the situation objectively and proposing sensible and practical measures, it has degenerated into a left-wing feminist pamphlet. in addition to the total disregard for the subsidiarity of the competence of the member states, it calls for mandatory quotas for women in management positions (board members, supervisory boards, etc.). the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. it must be left to the firms and other organizations, offices and parties to decide who they will appoint to a particular function. the first and foremost criterion should therefore be qualifications and not gender. quotas for electoral lists in eu, national or regional elections are neither really practical nor meaningful, as there is no universal proportional representation in europe. the commission has also proposed that the council should be able to adopt a decision on the basis of the results of the consultations. the various parties also have different structures and structures. a party with a majority of women will therefore also field more women and vice versa. in conclusion, therefore, it can be said that in this area too, supply and demand will ultimately produce a good result, and not coercive measures dictated by the eu, which is why i rejected the report.
in writing. - i cannot agree with the report in any way and there are actually 3 really scientific studies from universities since last year, namely the university of konstanz, the university of michigan and the university of cologne, which prove that: 1. companies with diversity in the top positions are not better, 2. the quota, for example in norway, causes considerable damage to the companies concerned, and 3. a quota in both the private sector and the public service is a violation of the law in force, in this sense i voted against the report. quotas risk pushing back the principle of equal treatment, because for me, any form of quota is discriminatory. quota regulation is also counterproductive, because it leads to highly qualified women being labelled as quota women. in the case of recruitment, qualifications alone should be the deciding factor, not gender.
in writing. − the promotion of the equal participation of women and men in power and decision-making to eliminate discrimination against women in political and public life as well as the adoption of ‘temporary special measures aimed at accelerating de facto equality between men and women’ are in the focus of this report. in the view of the rapporteur it is important to promote the presence of women from different backgrounds in decision-making positions, therefore this report has to be supported.
in writing. - membership of a cooperative creates a mutual obligation of loyalty between the cooperative and the member. in the case of cooperatives, there have been recent interesting developments and court decisions which have highlighted a whole range of practical problems, for example in the case of housing cooperatives. the case law in individual cases varies widely. there are problems, for example, with regard to the question of continuing a tenancy when the user of the cooperative apartment loses his membership or when cooperative apartments are sold to municipal or even private housing companies. the present report does not address these developments or does not address them sufficiently, which is why i did not approve it.
in writing. − this report highlights that cooperative societies should be one of the instruments to overcome the actual situation of crisis in europe. however, it has not been a success, and on top of that, some member states have not transposed articles of the directive referring to employees’ rights, including the gender-specific provisions. the cooperatives should be enhanced as also the involvement of its employees in order to strengthen europe’s economy.
in writing. − intergovernmental cooperation and various strategies are intended to provide incentives for an open european higher education area. in fact, however, there are a number of difficulties whose solutions are still unresolved. for example, the netherlands demands financial compensation for the many german students at dutch universities. austria has also raised problems in this respect in the council. hungary has registered a particular influx of german students in medical studies. germany, on the other hand, argues that it receives more students from other countries within the eu than it exports. the establishment of quotas to prevent an influx of students from eu countries was criticised by the ecj as unlawful. in view of the overwhelming number of courses, the bologna process cannot be based on the idea that students who would not be able to enter university in their own country should move to other countries and take the place of domestic students. i have therefore abstained on this report.
in writing. - the bologna process has been effectively stalled for several years. the single european education area remains a vision and it is time to take concrete action on the recognition of qualifications. this also requires encouraging mobility within national university systems, as in austria, for example, a student's academic results are often recognised in one state but not in another. the bologna process cannot be achieved without additional costs, i.e. financial support for universities. the money was to be used to develop national education systems to exploit the full potential of the european higher education area. in addition, there is an urgent need to reduce bureaucratic obstacles, such as the use of the numerus clausus for admission to charité university berlin, as well as relevant subjects (physics, biology, mathematics) taken in the last two years of schooling. however, these additional points are only recognised if the attendance of the subjects is attested by the school leaving certificate itself. additional official certificates are not recognised for purely bureaucratic and discriminatory reasons. the fact that austrian and french school diplomas do not contain this information means that students from these countries are placed in a worse position and are thus discriminated against. i shall abstain on this point because it is not dealt with in the report.
in writing. − the report on quality management for european statistics stresses the urgent necessity to provide better quality statistics within the eu. it is extremely necessary to enforce a european statistics code of practice, in order to have impartial, transparent and objective statistics not only at an eu level but also at a national level in cooperation with national bodies. as this report also establishes more user-friendly publications to help citizens understand statistics, i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. − this motion for a resolution takes into account the fact that the ilo estimates that more than 215 million children worldwide are child labourers; that 70 % of world cocoa production is cultivated in west africa and all family members, including children, are involved in this work; that children working in ghana and côte d’ivoire are exposed to different types of danger; and that there are many programmes and initiatives to combat such child exploitation. having regard to all this information the parliament urges those states which have yet to ratify the un convention on the rights of the child or ilo conventions nos 138 or 182 to ratify them urgently; urges all stakeholders to live up to their responsibilities in terms of combating all forms of forced child labour and trafficking; urges the commission to ensure that all trade agreements include effective provisions on poverty reduction and the promotion of decent work and safe working conditions, along with legally binding clauses on internationally agreed human rights; welcomes all initiatives to promote best practice and calls on the international cocoa agreement partners to look into the possibility of introducing accredited, third-party-audited traceability for the cocoa supply chain.
in writing. − the cocoa sector is the livelihood of 50 million people worldwide. transparency and sustainability must therefore be further promoted in this sector of the economy. the cocoa agreement promotes fair prices that provide producers and consumers in the cocoa value chain with a fair income. it also aims to increase transparency in the global cocoa industry by compiling and analysing relevant statistics and studies. on 25 june 2010, the united nations cocoa conference, which includes the main cocoa producing and consuming countries, agreed on the cocoa agreement of 2010, which is intended to replace the agreement of 2001. the new convention will be valid for 10 years and may be renewed twice for a period of two years. the 2010 convention aims to create the conditions for a fairer and more sustainable global cocoa trade. that is why i voted in favour of the report.

the fact that most of its water is salt water. the water reserves amount to 1.4 billion cubic kilometres, of which only 2.5% is usable fresh water. most of this fresh water is stored in groundwater and we have only 1% of it available for actual human consumption. that's two hundred thousand cubic kilometers. 60% are already in use. and if we see that global water consumption is increasing at in writing. - emission trading is a dubious instrument of environmental policy aimed at reducing emissions. in the european union, the eu emissions trading system for carbon dioxide emissions was introduced by law in 2005. emissions trading links greenhouse gas emissions to the possession of allowances: each greenhouse gas emitter is only allowed to release the amount of pollutants for which it holds emission allowances. if fewer pollutants are released than permitted, excess rights can be resold. on the other hand, those responsible for releasing too many greenhouse gases can buy emission rights. there are also generous exemptions from the state. all this opens the door to speculation and misses the real purpose of the regulation, which is to reduce co2 emissions. the high level of emission trading is therefore not conducive to investment in the creation of a low-carbon economy. the report also contains a number of important recommendations, including the need to ensure that the commission's proposals are implemented.
in writing. − as a matter of principle, emissions trading starts with a cap on greenhouse gases. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to finance the necessary measures. those countries whose emissions are below the ceiling can buy excess allowances. on the other hand, countries that emit greenhouse gases beyond the cap can buy these emission allowances. since the allowances are tradable on the open market, the price is determined by supply and demand. the issue of emission allowance trading is problematic in several ways: the market is not transparent, speculators manipulate the prices on the trading platforms. in addition, some of the alleged environmental projects in emerging countries are supported, the climate impact of these projects is systematically overestimated, and many of them are even counterproductive. in conclusion, i do not think that the high level of emissions trading is supporting investment in low-carbon technologies. but this would be urgently needed to reduce the greenhouse effect. that is why i voted against the report.

in writing. − in principle, the eu has strengthened travellers' rights in recent years. although there are regulations for air travellers, the question of whether airlines must compensate their guests for long delays in a lump sum is still controversial. the european court of justice is also considering a case on this matter. airlines refuse to pay compensation in the event of 'extraordinary circumstances', citing an international obligation to provide hotel and meals to passengers in the event of delays, but not to pay compensation. the question whether an airline is obliged to compensate passengers who miss their connecting flight because of a delay is also controversial. it is therefore important that the eu address this issue once again, although there are still some unresolved issues, such as the strict safety rules. i have taken this into account in my voting behaviour.

in writing. − citizenship of the union establishes a legal relationship between the citizen and the union, which includes rights and obligations. these rights include freedom of movement, non-discrimination, the right to vote in local elections, the right to vote in the european parliament, diplomatic and consular protection, the right to petition and to lodge a complaint, and the right to communicate with the eu in one of the official languages of the european union and to receive a reply in the same language. the 'union citizenship report 2010' has shown that citizens of the european union are above all exercising their right to free movement. this means that every citizen of the union has the fundamental right to move freely within the european union, to enter and reside in any other member state. however, this right of residence may be restricted in order to safeguard the legitimate interests of the member states. i did not vote for the report because i believe that national rules, especially those concerning the residence permit of third-country nationals, should not be overridden by a transposed union law.

in writing. if you normally work in several european member states, you should be covered by social security wherever you have your main place of residence. the new regulation on the coordination of social security systems is designed to fill existing gaps and to take account of changes in national legislation. the new rules are particularly important for flight attendants and selfemployed border crossers. the social security system is and will of course remain a matter for the individual member states. but we are also making sure that these systems remain applicable and fair to those people who work in several eu countries because of increased mobility. it should not be decisive where the registered office of the company is, it is decisive for social security the "home base", i.e. the centre of life from which departure usually takes place. the commission has also proposed that the commission should be given the task of drawing up a report on the implementation of the directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. we're gonna put a stop to that. this is a new regulation of the european internal market which does not allow dumping of social security systems and provides for a higher level of legal certainty. we have thus moved closer to a more social europe.

in writing. − social security can be defined as any social protection system established by law or other binding regulation which provides a certain level of income security to individuals facing risks such as old age, survivorship, incapacity for work, disability, unemployment or childcare. it can also provide access to medical treatment or prevention. social security, as defined by the international social security association, includes social insurance schemes, social assistance programmes, universal schemes, mutual aid schemes, national pension funds and other forms, including market-oriented concepts, which are part of a country's social security system according to national legislation or practice. since 1 may 2010, regulations (ec) no 883/2004 and 987/2009 on the coordination of social security systems have been applicable in all eu member states. in order to ensure adequate coordination of national social security systems at eu level, this regulation should be adapted. i have abstained because the report does not make it clear what improvement could be achieved by amending the regulation.

in writing. − the modernised social security regulations resulting especially from the increase in negotiations between member states are of high importance to the european union and its citizens and therefore this report has to be supported, which i did by my vote in favour. the need for modernisation came, among other things, from changes in national legislation and from the case law of the court of justice of the european union. member states frequently amend their national social security legislation. as a consequence, the references made to national legislation in eu legislation coordinating social security systems can become outdated; this will create legal uncertainty for stakeholders when applying the regulations. the references in the regulations therefore need to be updated so that they correctly reflect legal changes at national level and changes in social reality.

member of the commission. − mr president, i wish to thank the honourable members and mrs astrid lulling for the report and for the speedy and thorough treatment of this proposal. its main purposes are to meet the eu’s priority goals of combating climate change, improving energy efficiency, stimulating renewable energy sources and ensuring fair competition within the internal market. to achieve this, the proposal bases taxation on objective criteria – co2 emissions and energy content. this will offer many advantages. first, taxation of energy products will be more coherent. second, consumers will receive a consistent price signal to reduce emissions and to save energy. third, double taxation and overlaps with the eu emission trading scheme will be removed. fourth, use of sustainable biofuels and products from biomass will be promoted, since they will be exempt from co2 taxation. last but not least, taxes on polluting activities are a means of shifting taxation away from labour, thereby supporting growth and competiveness. the impact of such far-reaching changes is addressed by providing for transitional periods up to 2023, when appropriate. turning to the amendments, the commission welcomes the support for the main features of its proposal, in particular the introduction of a co2- and energy-related element, a gradual increase of minimum rates by 2018 and the principle of equal taxation of all fuels put to the same use. the commission would insist on keeping the ‘proportionality principle’, which means equal taxation of petrol and diesel. there is no reason to subsidise the use of diesel over the use of petrol. the impact on demand for diesel cars should not be overestimated: the efficiency of conversion technology in current diesel cars is higher than in petrol cars, and it would still remain attractive to purchase diesel cars. moreover, long transitional periods should ensure time to adjust. it is neither the cars of today nor the cars of tomorrow that are at stake. it is the cars of our children or even our grandchildren. i would like to reassure you that many of the amendments accepted by the committee on economic and monetary affairs concern issues which are already covered by the proposal and do not require changes to it. the commission will continue to defend the spirit of those issues in the negotiations in the council. the commission understands the call for longer transitional periods, particularly in terms of respecting the principle of equal taxation, and would support them in the council, as part of an overall compromise. it would insist on keeping automatic indexation in order to keep the agreed level of rate harmonisation intact and to avoid an erosion of member states’ revenue by inflation. the commission could accept an automatic alignment of the minimum co2 tax level to the price of ets allowances, if a legally-sound reference index can be referred to. the commission welcomes the phasing-out of the tax advantage for commercial diesel in order to achieve full internalisation of external costs. the commission does not, however, see the need for a specific transitional period for this. long transitional periods up to 2023 are already provided for and could be extended until 2025 in the context of an overall compromise in the council. as for energy consumption by households, the commission is not now in favour of agreeing on an end date for phasing out optional tax exemptions or reductions. it also feels that it would be premature to remove the exemption for commercial aircraft and shipping fuel now, taking into account the fact that the aviation sector is covered by the eu ets and that developments on tackling emissions in the maritime sector could take place in the near future. both these issues will in any case be reviewed in the regular commission report on the application of the new framework for energy taxation. in conclusion, the commission is open to discuss amendments to its proposal, provided that they do not undermine its main objectives and that they preserve its key principles.

in writing. the rome ii regulation determines the law applicable to non-contractual obligations where more than one member state is involved. this includes, for example, product liability or culpa in contrahendo. in principle, the regulation provides that either the law of the state in which the damage occurs or the law of the state in which the injured person is habitually resident is to apply. but rome ii does not apply to cases relating to the protection of privacy and freedom of expression. the increased use of the internet has led to a number of cross-border situations. rome ii does not in principle harmonise substantive law: the regulation contains conflict-of-law rules which make it possible to determine the applicable law. the commission has also proposed that the member states should be required to provide for the possibility of a review of the provisions of the directive in the light of the new provisions. this balance must be respected in the spirit of the principle of subsidiarity.

in writing. - the rome ii regulation determines the law applicable to non-contractual obligations - where more than one member state is involved. this includes, for example, product liability or culpa in contrahendo. in principle, the regulation provides that either the law of the state in which the damage occurs or the law of the state in which the injured person is habitually resident is to apply. but rome ii does not apply to cases relating to the protection of privacy and freedom of expression. the increased use of the internet has led to a number of cross-border situations. rome ii does not in principle constitute harmonisation of substantive law: the regulation contains conflict-of-law rules which make it possible to determine the applicable law. the commission has also proposed that the member states should be required to provide for the possibility of a review of the provisions of the directive in the light of the new provisions. this balance must be respected in the spirit of the principle of subsidiarity. i voted accordingly.

in writing. − the lisbon treaty and the abandoning of the pillar structure simplified the path to the development of eu criminal law in the context of the eu as an area of freedom, security and justice. the report highlights the principles of criminal law (principle of individual guilt, legal certainty, non retroactivity, ne bis in idem and presumption of innocence). moreover, judicial cooperation in criminal law is based on the principle of mutual recognition. to fully apply this principle, some flanking measures are needed to develop and legitimate ‘mutual trust’ – within an eu common criminal legal culture. among these measures are harmonisation of substantive criminal law (crimes and sanctions) and common uniform minimum standards of protection for suspects and defendants in criminal proceedings and therefore this report has to be supported, which i did by my vote in favour.
in writing. − a uniform level of consumer protection should be provided within the eu, in particular in terms of protection against unfair commercial practices, misleading advertising and abusive contractual clauses. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. the lack of knowledge of the national language, the lack of knowledge or the imperative need to use new technologies with which the consumer concerned is not familiar also constitute a particular case for protection. protection must not only focus on economic interest but also cover other areas such as health and safety. in particular, there are still problems with enforcement in relation to breaches of information obligations and the right of withdrawal, particularly in cross-border online purchases. the financial sector remains problematic in its complexity. the commission has also taken into account the fact that the airport operator has not yet been able to demonstrate that it is able to comply with the conditions for the granting of the aid. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the consumer is able to benefit from the new rules. that is why i could not agree to the report.

in writing. − this directive provides for the introduction of a financial transaction tax. the aims are to generate substantial revenue and to create a disincentive to highly leveraged and harmful speculative transactions. the tax covers all transactions by eu-resident financial institutions. the tax rates will be around 0.1% for shares and bonds and 0.01% for derivatives. the commission’s proposal includes no direct references to the management of the revenues.

in writing. for months now, the european parliament has been negotiating the so-called schengen package under the ordinary legislative procedure. the ministers of the interior have now, by surprise, changed the legal basis (article 70) and aim to transfer responsibility to the nation states. this question, which may seem technical, is the fundamental question of all european politics: should the community and its institutions decide on the basis of community principles or should national governments decide on the basis of positions more or less agreed upon jointly - that is, at community or intergovernmental level? since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the european parliament has become increasingly a body that transcends national interests. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft budget for the financial year. the european interior ministers are clearly afraid that parliament is playing its role as guardian of european fundamental rights.

in writing. - as early as 1964, some developing countries were calling for trade preferences to improve their economic situation. the first step in the process of liberalization of trade in goods was taken in 1968 with the conclusion of an agreement establishing a system of generalized tariff preferences (gsp). in 1971 the european economic community introduced gsp, and other countries such as the united states followed suit. the temporary granting of trade preferences has been designed to increase the export earnings of developing countries by diversifying export products, to promote industrialization and to accelerate the economic growth of developing countries. the gsp should also ensure that the products benefiting from the scheme originate in developing countries. to date, the gsp is one of the eu's most important instruments in the field of trade and is monitored by the european commission. i am sorry to say that i cannot agree with the report because the proposed amendments do not seem to have matured.

in writing. − the inclusion of russia in the wto will allow the opening of the russian market to foreign services; russia will grant more favourable treatment than before to foreign suppliers in eleven sectors covering, inter alia, professional services, construction, telecommunications and financial services. we must not forget that currently trade in services represents approximately 20% of european exports to russia. this means that the eu has a special interest in signing this agreement to keep the commitments that the eu is already enjoying; russia’s commitments will not only create additional business opportunities for european companies, but will also improve the situation of european exporters and investors currently working with russia.

in writing. − the fact of russia joining the world trade organization has not prevented the maintenance of some trade-distorting measures, among them the requirement that foreign car manufacturers are located in russia, encouraging job creation, in return for privileges related to the importation of car parts – a situation that certainly hurts european industry. although the deadline to remove this measure is july 2018, the eu has negotiated a bilateral agreement to provide a mechanism for compensating eu producers or automotive components that are affected by a possible decline in exports to russia.
in writing. − this agreement commits russia not to impose additional export duties on raw materials. this obligation applies to a number of raw materials listed in the agreement. this is a clear advantage for european smes. however, greater attention must be paid to a follow-up agreement. i am in favour of this agreement and have therefore agreed to it.
in writing. − the main benefit is russia's commitment that no export duty will be imposed or increased on these raw materials. if russia still wishes to do so, it should consult the european commission at least two months in advance. at the same time, the ep report also contains some criticism of the agreement. first, russia only undertakes to 'do its best' and 'consult' with the commission. such wording is not sufficiently binding. second, the agreement does not provide for a bilateral dispute settlement mechanism. the agreement is therefore to be considered as a temporary solution. a more legally binding agreement should be concluded and incorporated into the new russia-eu partnership and cooperation agreement. while the agreement does not completely rule out unexpected actions by russian partners, it is an important guarantee that economic relations with russia will enter a more stable and predictable phase. as rapporteur for the ep, i called on my colleagues to support the agreement and i voted in favour. i consider this to be a positive interim solution until a more legally binding agreement is reached.
in writing. − in the context of its accession to the world trade organization, the russian federation has pledged to reduce or phase out its current export duties for a list of raw materials. however, the list does not prevent the establishment of export duties on new or additional materials not included on it. among such materials are agricultural products and seeds, tobacco, chemicals, ferrous metals and energy minerals, etcetera – all materials very important for eu. the eu has negotiated this agreement with russia to avoid the establishment of new restrictions on export duties. under the bilateral agreement the russian government is committed to doing everything possible not to introduce or increase export duties for raw materials listed in the agreement; in this way, if russia wants to apply export duties on such products, it will consult the commission.

in writing. − the protection of intellectual property is a legitimate concern, especially as it also affects europe's competitiveness. the participating nations or associations of states want to establish international standards in the fight against product piracy and copyright infringement with acta. however, it is feared that this may also severely restrict the freedom of individuals on the internet. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the directive is implemented. internet service providers would be de facto obliged to monitor their customers' data traffic and report any errors immediately. i voted against acta because it is still unclear how privacy can be guaranteed. the commission is also concerned about the massive restrictions on freedom of information on the internet. it is also impossible that a subject which is really intended to concern every citizen should be discussed in private. the acta agreement has a number of pitfalls, including a number of vague provisions that can open the door to abuse.
in writing. − acta is a plurilateral agreement negotiated between the eu, the us, australia, canada, japan, mexico, morocco, new zealand, singapore, south korea and switzerland aiming at preventing trade in counterfeit physical and digital goods by enforcing ipr. opposition to acta: - few positive effects because the countries in most counterfeit goods originate (china) are not a party; - goes beyond eu acquis and breaks the balance between ipr protection and fundamental rights such as right to information and education, freedom of expression, rights accessible healthcare, protection of privacy and data protection, etc. to that end, the agreement introduces the possibility for states to introduce laws forcing isps to disclose information about subscribers with a simple allegation by a right-holder for such disclosure. moreover, the agreement introduces criminal sanctions for ‘commercial scale’ infringements and this without a proper definition of the term ‘commercial’. the agreement could also compromise the export of generic medicines to poorer countries. inta, which led parliament’s scrutiny of acta, and 4 other committees (civil liberties, industry, legal affairs and development) recommended that parliament should reject the agreement. since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the ep should give its consent to international agreements.

in writing. − the sulphur content of marine fuels in eu waters is to be set at a maximum of 0.5% from 2015 onwards, and in sox emission monitoring areas (seca) the value is to be reduced to 0.1%. these measures, according to experts, are intended to significantly improve air quality, especially in coastal areas. however, the changeover would impose high costs on shipping companies and risk shifting some of the shipping traffic to inland waterways. this is in contrast to another eu measure, namely to handle more transport by water or rail than by road. coastal and inland waterway vessels consume much less fuel per transport unit and emit correspondingly less carbon dioxide than lorries. the eu therefore wants to put a third of what is transported by truck over 300 kilometres by rail or ship by 2030. similar measures to those for onshore factories are being considered for ships to clean up the exhaust gases. the commission has already proposed a number of measures to improve the efficiency of the gas treatment system. i voted in favour of the report because the rapporteur has clearly mentioned the possibilities of financing and financial support for shipping companies. the proposed granting of state aid for investment seems to me to be an appropriate means of doing so.
in writing. − the proposed changes are intended to achieve significant benefits for health and the environment, while at the same time levelling costs. the air quality in coastal areas in particular will therefore improve considerably. as the commission estimates that the monetary health benefits will outweigh the cost of reducing emissions from ships by a factor of 225 and the health benefits will amount to eur 816 billion, while the costs are estimated by the commission to be only eur 0.63.7 billion, i welcome the proposed amendments and vote in favour of the report.
in writing. - the report shows that it is essential to put into practice the maximum sulphur limits for fuel. this decision is important for the environment and may be the most important health-related innovation in the current election period. the use of exhaust gas cleaning equipment should be encouraged and supported. emissions should also be reduced by alternative methods (see also liquefied natural gas, liquefied natural gas (lng)).

directives set minimum european standards. there must be no exceptions for micro-enterprises or smes. on the contrary, member states can and should provide for greater protection for workers in their the commission is therefore proposing to extend the period of validity of the directive to the period of 1 january 1999. the commission is not i would like to thank the rapporteur very much. better legislation is an extremely important issue in the european context, precisely because - and this is also the media coverage, so to speak - european laws are considered extremely complicated, incomprehensible and difficult to understand and apply. however, and i want to emphasize this very clearly here, this is also due in large part to the implementation in the member states. the experience of recent years has shown that european regulations are often used to solve national problems that have not been solved elsewhere. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. this is an essential and important element. we must also make a much greater effort to deal with this aspect in the context of the implementation of community law. the second point which i think is important - and the rapporteur has focused very much on this - is the question of impact assessments. i agree with him that political decisions should also be based on facts. there is nothing wrong with that. however, impact assessments can also be used very well in policy. let me give you an example. when there was an impact assessment on the introduction of megatraks, these giant trucks, on european roads, the commission took an impact assessment that looked primarily at whether large companies would make more profit, but not how much more public spending this would mean. this means that an impact assessment always depends on the criteria. if we hide political beliefs behind official impact assessments, we are not doing the good law making any good either.

in writing. − the agreement on scientific and technological cooperation (stc) between the european community and the federative republic of brazil entered into force in 2007 for the first time for a period of five years. the agreement is intended to facilitate cooperation and the exchange of scientific research between the eu and brazil. the aim is to develop joint research projects that will benefit both sides. since there is no clear cost-benefit breakdown of the latest agreement between the eu and brazil, i am not sure that it would actually make sense to extend the agreement, which is costing the eu a lot of money. that is why i abstained.

in writing. − the smart regulation agenda seeks to build on the efforts to improve legislation, simplify eu legislation and reduce administrative and regulatory burdens. the agenda offers a new opportunity for the eu institutions to fully implement good governance based on evidence-based policy making, with impact assessments and ex-post controls as key elements. the 2003 interinstitutional agreement on better law-making needs to be adapted to the current legal environment created by the lisbon treaty. in principle, the revision of the subsidiarity controls is to be welcomed. the report does not, however, cover the attempt to eliminate national competences at eu level through back doors. i have taken these considerations into account in my voting behaviour.

in writing. − in 2012 and 2013, the atlantic partners will work together to develop an action plan under the european maritime strategy for the atlantic. there is nothing inherently wrong with this approach. however, it is not possible to avoid the suspicion that the eu should be used primarily for financial support. the chances of success of the desired synergy effects may be called into question on the basis of past experience. to date, all marine strategies have not been particularly successful. the commission has not yet succeeded in ensuring that existing policies, such as those relating to marine surveillance and overfishing, are respected. i think that the strategy for the atlantic area within the framework of cohesion policy is an unworkable wish-fulfillment which will cost a lot of money at most, and i voted accordingly.
in writing. − the argument that a reliable energy supply is best secured by a functioning internal energy market is not borne out by the experience of the consequences of energy market liberalisation efforts and privatisation problems in general. the much-vaunted reductions in electricity prices that liberalization is supposed to bring are not noticed by the final consumer. the bills of the energy companies are so complex that they are almost impossible to compare. this may be one of the main reasons why, contrary to forecasts, few consumers actually switched suppliers. i can only agree with a few of the statements in the report, such as the concern about the eu's continued high energy dependence. i cannot agree with the report in sum.
in writing. the report favours extending the commission's powers with regard to intergovernmental agreements between third countries and eu member states. the commission should be present in future in negotiations between a member state and a third country in the field of energy policy, according to the report. the commission has already made a number of proposals in this area. energy policy in the eu is not uniform and accordingly the requirements in an intergovernmental agreement will be completely different. for this reason, member states should continue to be able to negotiate on their own responsibility and alone. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. - european agricultural products are among the highest quality in the world. this is partly due to the long tradition of agriculture and the optimisation of the tools used. to ensure that consumers are assured of the origin and content of their products, there are european-wide quality labels such as protected designation of origin (pdo), protected geographical indication (pgi), traditional speciality guaranteed (tsg), organic farming and outermost regions. as the end user still has some difficulties in navigating through the jungle of information on the products concerned, i agree with the rapporteur that we should aim for greater clarity and also simplification. first of all, the quality scheme for traditional specialities guaranteed should apply to all processed products. i also agree with the rapporteur that it is necessary to define clearly what is meant by production steps. the introduction of a seal valid throughout the eu, which can only be used on products which have undergone the same registration procedure under the same conditions, would also be welcome. i therefore voted in favour of the report.

in writing. − the eu has created quality labels (pgi, pgi, pgi) for high-quality regional food. in order to provide greater clarity for producers, clear definitions of terms and a simplification of the entire text should be introduced. in addition, additional and well-defined product groups are included to create added value for both consumers and producers. i have agreed to this report.
in writing. − social enterprises are defined as those that have a positive social impact and whose purpose is primarily social rather than profit-maximising. although social enterprises often receive public funding, investment through private funds that invest in social enterprises in a targeted way remains essential for their growth. such social investment funds are rare. cross-border investment in such funds is proving to be complex and expensive. the european funds are intended to help overcome the chronic shortage of funding for enterprises and social entrepreneurship initiatives. the funds are intended to be used only by companies which use their profits to achieve their social objectives. the aim is to open the fund to institutional investors and wealthy individuals. experience with micro-credit, among other things, has shown that well-intentioned social projects, when heavily involved in the private sector, can develop an uncontrollable dynamic that is the direct victim of those who should have benefited. in this respect, the proposal seems to me to be too little thought out and i cannot therefore agree with it.
in writing. − orphan works are works whose rightsholders cannot be identified or traced. to date, libraries that have digitized such works are not allowed to make them available to the public because the question of authorship cannot be clarified. consequently, the non-commercial use of orphan works is not possible either. in addition, there is no europe-wide regulation on this subject, which means that the accessibility of orphan works differs from one member state to another, which brings significant disadvantages for the individual user. the eu is also at a significant competitive disadvantage in the online market, following a court decision in the us that gives 'google books' the legitimacy to publish orphan works. intellectual property is a commodity that needs to be protected, especially in the age of online media. the report suggests that the orphan status of a work can be lifted if an author reports legitimate copyright infringements through publication. i voted in favour of the report because i believe that it is time to create legal certainty for users on the internet, which goes beyond the borders of individual member states.
in writing. − orphan works, i.e. works of unknown authorship, have the problem of not being published. even non-commercial use is prohibited unless the author gives his consent. the report favours the publication of orphan works for non-commercial use in all member states. this would allow citizens legal access to the content of these works. the eu-wide availability of orphan works would promote europe's cultural diversity and provide an additional source of knowledge and learning. if the author is found, the status of 'orphan work' could be revoked. on the other hand, many questions remain about copyright. the question of the author's remuneration and the possible harmonization of the databases of the member states have not yet been settled. that's why i abstained.

draft opinion of the consultative committee on employment and social affairs. mr president, i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. i would like to begin by thanking the two years of negotiations that we have had, in particular the persistent and patient rapporteur, mr zwiefka, for his way of conducting the negotiations, but also the presidency, which is unfortunately not here at the moment, the cypriot presidency, and the danish and polish presidencies before that, which have worked very constructively. the revolution announced is not the result; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. the regulation on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters within the eu was already one of the best-functioning model regulations in the european internal market before this revision. i would like to highlight some positive points which are particularly important for my group, the s&ds. first, there are clear rules on access to justice and the enforcement of individual rights, which is important for citizens, businesses and the functioning of the internal market as a whole. the abolition of the exequatur procedure was, of course, the main task we accomplished, and despite initial doubts we have now succeeded in achieving this abolition. the extension of the regulation to third countries will be decided, albeit not as intended by the european commission in all cases, but at least in consumer matters and in matters concerning individual employment contracts, in order to protect the weaker party. this is very important. the negotiations on this regulation have been going on since the green paper of 2009, that is, since the beginning of the legislative period, and the new version has been under discussion for at least two years. it is very strange to me that the commission has presented the revision as a new version. the new wording is intended, in my view, to simplify the procedure for non-controversial matters and to speed up the procedures for adapting legislative texts. the brussels i is clearly not an uncontroversial issue, which resulted in the procedure being neither simple nor short. the only reason i can see why the commission has chosen the new version is to restrict the legislative power of parliament, but also of the council. i think that is very worrying from a democratic point of view. i therefore ask that the interinstitutional agreement with the commission be revised in this respect. it is not acceptable for the executive to restrict legislation in this way, even if it is proposing profound changes to the regulation. and now the most important thing for me, which comes to the end. as regards the future of the brussels i regulation, as the author of the opinion of the commission's employment committee, i recommend that a jurisdiction for industrial action be introduced to avoid the delay of proceedings resulting from strikes. moreover, it would finally bring the procedural law into line with the law materially applicable. the rome ii regulation governs the law applicable to cross-border claims. this provides that the law of industrial action is to be applied in cases of damage in connection with strikes. and why should this not apply to jurisdiction? i ask the commission to take this into account. we in the european parliament will certainly take care of that. a writer. mr president, i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. i am speaking for the legal affairs committee, now also in the direction of mr stoyanov. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is of particular importance in that it allows children who have been wrongfully removed to be returned immediately to their last place of residence. the commission rightly considers that the decision on the accession of the eight countries, namely morocco, russia, andorra, seychelles, albania, gabon, singapore and armenia, is the exclusive competence of the european union. the european court of justice has also clarified that matters which clearly fall within the union's competence within the eu are also within the union's competence in external relations. in this case, the brussels iia regulation on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial matters and in matters of parental responsibility clearly gives us competence at union level. it is clear to everyone that the union has exclusive external competence in matters of international child abduction. in this respect, the legal affairs committee's message is primarily directed at the council. the council must end its blockade on this important matter without delay. the european parliament should also be consulted. we as members of parliament, elected by the people, are constantly confronted with these problems. who, if not the european parliament, is concerned with the concerns of the citizens? the committee on legal affairs and citizens' rights also sees no reason why these countries should not join. the best interests of the child must always come first. national vanities are totally inappropriate in these cases. the commission is therefore asked why the council can block such an important decision. the accession of these eight countries is of the utmost importance. the importance of accession is shown by many tragic cases reported in the media, including one of alleged child abduction in the country i know best, my native austria. this case, although not concerned with relations with a third country, illustrates the family tragedies that can occur. little oliver weilharter is currently with his father in denmark. the mother and grandparents in austria are worried that oliver will not be allowed to return to austria. the main issues are two judgments of different wording from denmark and austria concerning the wrongful removal of the child. the hague convention on child abduction is not applicable in this case because the danish courts do not consider the father's conduct to be child abduction. however, the same problem arises with the brussels iia regulation, as this regulation is not binding on denmark. in particular, with regard to the candidate countries of russia and morocco, many eu citizens have family ties to these countries. similar cases can be avoided and combated by the accession of these countries. the example of oliver therefore shows that the accession of the eight countries is essential for the well-being of children.
the commission is therefore proposing to extend the period of validity of the directive to the period of 1 january 1999. the commission is not the council's policy of delay is particularly reprehensible in this respect. kidnapping is a traumatic experience, for the children in any case, and often for the parents involved. i think everyone will agree that we must at least improve the legal possibilities so that the child can return as soon as possible to his place of origin and habitual residence. the hague convention is one such mechanism that protects and defends the rights of the child in such cases and provides assistance in bilateral cases of child abduction. we now have two partners in the queue: russia and morocco, where there are always dramatic cases and where there are always great difficulties in reaching agreements. we could make this problem easier for those involved tomorrow if the council - and let us be clear here - did not play a game of power which i do not approve of on a completely inappropriate field. the council does not want the european parliament to have a say in this. the council is not in agreement on certain issues, long negotiations - particularly with russia, for example - are not producing results, and we cannot give the help we could if the hague convention were applicable to these countries. it would be very interesting to know how many children and partners have already been harmed by these delays on the part of the council. i would appeal to the council to look for another example of blocking. this is about the fate of children! i would like to ask you to allow us to continue the procedure properly, with the participation of the european parliament.
mr president, i would like to thank mrs reding for her report. we are in very close contact with the case, i believe, of the young oliver weilharter, an austrian child who was abducted to denmark. i have to say that child abduction - whether it happens outside or inside the european union - is the worst crime. if we sit here and watch, and stand by and do nothing, we are wronging these children. i therefore urge that we take action here at international level, but also, of course, at european level. how can it work at international level if we cannot do it at european level?
