in writing. − the offshore protocol, adopted on 14 october 1994, is one of the protocols to the convention for the protection of the marine environment and the coastal areas of the mediterranean. the eu, all eu member states bordering the mediterranean sea and 14 other mediterranean countries are parties to the convention. the offshore protocol covers a wide range of exploration and exploitation activities in the mediterranean sea, including licensing requirements, disposal of abandoned or decommissioned installations, use and disposal of hazardous substances, liability and compensation issues and safety issues. the offshore protocol entered into force on 24 march 2011 after its ratification by the six contracting parties and has not yet been signed or ratified by the union. accession to the union shall require the consent of the european parliament. the accident could have far-reaching consequences for the economy and for sensitive ecosystems. a policy for the sustainable management of offshore oil and gas activities is urgently needed, including to protect the environment from pollution from the exploration and extraction of raw materials.

in writing. - i voted for the bové report because the high-quality food produced in europe under strict environmental, animal welfare and health conditions needs a strong future-oriented marketing. in addition to the current support for information initiatives, such as the school milk programme, i am advocating more ambitious measures to promote agricultural products. these help the agricultural sector to achieve its full potential in terms of economic growth, job creation and rural regeneration. the strengthening of promotion measures will also increase the competitiveness of european products on the world market, as the european model of food production based on diversity, quality, traditional production methods and geographical authenticity is increasingly in demand.
in writing. − to make the cap as efficient as possible, there are a number of market promotion instruments, such as support for operational programmes in the fruit and vegetables sector, support for the promotion of wine in non-eu countries, school fruit and milk programmes, or support for market promotion measures by producer groups. all these measures are now being used to bridge food crises. i voted for the report because i agree with the rapporteur that a new policy of support should be defined. it is also essential to draw consumers' attention to european agricultural products.

in writing. - the shadow banking system is essentially a system that exists alongside the traditional banking system and which is involved in the intermediation of loans. these are mainly hedge funds, money market funds, but also special purpose vehicles, i.e. institutions known for their risky business. the problem is that their transactions are not subject to financial market regulation. the annual report of the financial stability board states that shadow banks turned over $67 trillion (eur 52,6 trillion) in 2011. this has increased their turnover by eur 5 trillion compared to 2010. for its report, the fsb examined its 24 member states as well as chile. the 25 countries studied account for 90 percent of the world's capital. the fsb found that shadow banks accounted for 25% of all financial transactions last year. in 2007, the report said, the figure was 27 percent. the report has received my vote as i agree with the rapporteur that some of the companies and activities identified by the fsb as shadow banking have clear benefits for the regular economy and could promote economic growth. however, instruments should be created to ensure full transparency.
in writing. − as a result of the financial crisis (2007), the g20 introduced new regulatory measures to make the financial system more secure. since then, among other things, capital requirements for financial institutions have been tightened. despite these changes, a large part of credit intermediation is still not sufficiently supervised and regulated. shadow banking is carried out through companies or financial contracts that create a combination of banking-like functions but are outside the regulatory scope or are not subject to any regulatory regime. we must take action against shadow banking.
in writing. − the internet is increasingly becoming a gateway to another world. this is of course particularly attractive to children and young people. gaming platforms and social media sites are used heavily from the age of nine. but there are also many dangers lurking online, such as cyberbullying, which can have a drastic impact on the real lives of young people. in order to teach young people the proper use of the internet and its dangers, they need the information and instruction of adults such as parents or teachers. i abstained because i believe that the problems facing children and young people online are beyond the control of the authorities. there is no doubt that there must be clear definitions on the part of the state about the legality of various sites and actions, but the responsibility for the welfare of children still lies in the field of education.
in writing. − children and young people are spending more and more time online and are becoming more and more involved in media at an earlier age. surfing without protection and control carries risks such as massive privacy violations, health risks, addiction and addiction phenomena, etc. the protection of children must be ensured and the control of cybercrime must be ensured.

in writing. the report 'towards a genuine economic and monetary union' aims to further centralise and raise all issues relating to economic and monetary union at european level. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the member states are not involved. in total disregard of the circumstances, it has been quite clear since may 2010 that a common monetary union between states with different economic orientations and strengths, different cultural views, especially as regards tax policy, is not useful. the apparently simple response of the eu establishment to call for more centralisation, always and everywhere, is therefore a complete disregard for the facts. there is one positive aspect to the report: in calling for 'necessary treaty changes ... to ensure legal certainty and democratic legitimacy', he confirms that the measures taken so far, bilateral loans to greece, efsf, esm and the ecb's bond-buying programme, were not covered by the eu treaty and are therefore illegal! the report is bad, it points in the wrong direction and it should therefore be rejected in all its aspects.

the rapporteur. - mr president, i have to say something. the implementation of community law should be of great interest to every member of parliament. why would you do that? we are making rules here in a sophisticated procedure, which at present is usually no more than a reading in parliament, but involves extensive discussions in the committees, taking account of various opinions, contacting the council, negotiating with the council, compromising and taking decisions in the european parliament, rules which apply or are intended to apply to the whole of the european union. this is the "should" we're talking about. when we see the effort that goes into creating these laws, these european regulations, and then have to observe how this eu law is either not implemented at all or is applied and controlled in a lax manner in some member states, then this must make us think a lot. unfortunately, the member states of the european union have not necessarily become more inclined in recent years to emphasize the commonalities in europe rather than the differences and the common rules of the game. i could give you a number of examples. the important thing in this process is that we point out the non-implementation, the wrong implementation, the poor implementation or the non-control. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. we are now at a critical point, which the legal affairs committee and my report very clearly criticise. the commission has introduced a practice called the 'eu pilot' a few years ago, a pilot project whose main objective is to reduce the number of infringement procedures against member states. instead, an attempt is made to reach an agreement with the member state through informal means. there is nothing to object to for the time being. but if the complainant hears nothing from the commission but 'i have received your complaint' and then nothing for a long time, if he himself has no access to the knowledge of the progress of the non-implementation process he has called for, then something is wrong with the danish state. this is not how it's gonna work. we therefore call on the commission not to use soft law but to codify, in accordance with article 298 of the treaties, a regulated procedure which ultimately respects and takes seriously the rights of the complainant. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. we must ensure that they are also informed of this when they are already involved in defending the rights of the parliament, the legislator at european level, against their own member state. i therefore appeal to the commission, as i did last year, to take decisive steps to improve the situation of the complainants once and for all.
i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. the commission, as guardian of the treaties, is not always in a pleasant position in this role. the commission's role in monitoring the application of eu law and its power to bring infringement proceedings against member states is not universally popular, but it is one of the commission's most important tasks. in 2010, we had an eu acquis of 8 400 regulations and 2 000 directives. by the end of 2010, there were 2 100 breaches reported. this is less than last year, but it is still far too high. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union. the tables should make it clear which part of a directive is transposed by which national text. after 10 years of blocking by the council, it is good that there is now agreement and that member states are submitting correlation tables in certain cases. this will make it easier in future to check whether a directive has been correctly transposed in the member state concerned. this report by mrs lichtenberger puts citizens at the centre of european legislation. it is important for citizens to have legal certainty and to know what their rights are in the internal market. if they are affected or involved and have brought the infringement to the attention of the public, for example by means of a petition, they must be able to understand the procedures and receive the information that is important to them. we members of parliament are constantly faced with problems which are based solely on the poor transposition of eu law into national law. this problem must be further reduced in the future.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank you for your report. europe has an ageing population, with low birth rates and a longer life expectancy. according to the world health organization, people are considered old from the age of 65 onward. there is a clear gender imbalance at this age across the eu. 50.6 million of the more than 87 million are women. women outlive men in life expectancy, but they are also at higher risk of disease and are much more susceptible to it. it is therefore logical that we should find appropriate information strategies, because the consequences of inactive ageing are not only costing the individual woman a healthy life, but also society and individuals high costs in the medical and social fields.
in writing. the effects of aging cannot be cured by a few miracle pills. because as we age, our metabolism slows down, cell renewal slows down, the water content of our tissues decreases, and our body's own repair work doesn't go as smoothly as it used to. gender differences also play a role in the aging process. of the centenarians, up to 85 percent are female. but while women are more resistant to age-related, life-shortening diseases, their morbidity is increasing. in plain language, women do age considerably more than men, but their hormonal constitution and comparatively lower muscle mass make them more frail and needy when they reach advanced age. one factor that we should not forget about women's aging is the growing trend towards radical starvation cures, which are becoming more common among girls. diets that are one-sided or lack nutrition deprive the body of important nutrients and can impair development during adolescence and lead to age-related diseases later in life. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the matter.

in writing. − following the armed conflict with russia in 2008 and the impact of the global financial crisis, georgia is facing financial problems despite multi-million euro aid packages. the second tranche of eu macrofinancial assistance was designed to help georgia meet its external financing needs and was subject to strict conditionality. however, the money still does not seem to be used efficiently enough. however, this is unacceptable in view of the budgetary situation in the vast majority of eu countries. i am in favour of financial support for georgia in principle and have taken these considerations into account in my voting behaviour.
in writing. − the eu has been trying to adopt a single european patent system since 2000, but has failed largely because of the insurmountable language barrier. in principle, a unitary patent is welcome to strengthen the eu's innovation capacity in global competition, especially against the us and china. however, the proposed unified patent court would displace the experienced european patent courts in the member states and national intellectual property rights would give way to the eu authority. even if the quality were only approximately the same, the quantity would suffer. it is expected that a maximum of 25% of the current completion rates will be achieved. experts also expect a fivefold increase in costs and risks, so that smes, for example, will no longer be able to sue. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. the new european patent court is designed to bring national institutions in the field of industrial property rights to a halt. however, the competition between national patent offices and the national courts attached to them contributes significantly to the quality of the european courts. the aim is to create a completely new common patent court to replace the highly successful national patent courts, which have a tradition of more than a century. the quality and efficiency of the planned jurisdiction is more than doubtful. in a previously unpublished study by the eu commission of 7 november 2011, the commission itself admits that the new multinational court will at most achieve a turnover of around 25% of national courts. this case is just one in a long list of nonsense committed by fanatical eurocrats for whom the only way to get a regulation right is to get it from brussels. the brussels mania for centralisation is most evident in the misconstruction of the euro. it is sad that it is taking over more and more areas of life, destroying rational and tried-and-tested constructions. i therefore naturally voted against the report.
in writing. − the implementation of a stability mechanism and a safeguard clause for the import of bananas from central america into the european union is designed to ensure a stable and high-quality trade in fruit. at the same time, the quality of bananas is to be guaranteed for european consumers. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the eu-central america association agreement is the first bi-regional association agreement signed by the eu since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty. the development of eu-latin america association relations is mutually beneficial and brings benefits to all. after all, the eu is the main investor and second largest trading partner in central america, as well as the largest donor of development aid. the agreement may also be suitable for contributing to greater regional integration and stability in central america. nevertheless, there are concerns about the negative impact of the new rules on the economic situation of the local economy in latin america. i have abstained because there are serious and well-founded concerns.
in writing. − the eu's association agreement with the latin american countries is the first bi-regional association agreement since the lisbon treaty and is designed to benefit both sides. the benefits for latin america are questionable, as most central american exports under the gsp+ already have duty-free access to the eu, and their trade policy room to develop their own development strategies that benefit the poor is likely to be limited. that is why i voted against the report.
in writing. the central american region has become one of the european union's most important trading partners. with trade in goods worth €174 billion and services worth €44 billion, it is in the european parliament's interest to further remove existing trade barriers. the aim is to promote the conservation of resources by introducing quality standards to protect consumers and producers and by targeting the modernisation of agriculture and industry. the protection of human rights is a top priority for the european parliament. article 355 of the convention provides for the possibility of suspending the convention in the event of human rights violations. the agreement therefore not only further promotes and intensifies trade, which is of economic importance to the european union, but also guarantees the protection of fundamental human rights. that is why i voted for the agreement.
in writing. - in order to guarantee consumers throughout the european union high-quality protection and quality when importing bananas from colombia and peru, i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of a stabilisation mechanism and a safeguard clause.
in writing. − in 2012, a trade agreement was concluded between the eu and colombia and peru. the agreement provides, inter alia, for the reduction and ultimately the elimination of customs duties in bilateral trade between the partners. it also contains a safeguard clause allowing tariff preferences to be suspended or withdrawn, very similar to the free trade agreement with the republic of korea, but with two differences in terms of the volume of bananas released and the special treatment of less-favoured areas. furthermore, the convention does not contain any provisions on customs refunds and no sensitive sectors are listed. the commission has also avoided parliamentary concerns such as provisions on monitoring and reporting or the role of trade unions and ngos. that is why i abstained.
in writing. - peru and colombia are important trading partners for the european union. the implementation of the agreement is expected to result in an annual relief of eur 270 million in customs duties on eu exports. the aim is to intensify trade to the benefit of both parties by eliminating customs barriers, improving access to services and investment and improving access to public procurement. this will facilitate the movement of goods and bring benefits to both sides. the european parliament attaches great importance to the protection and observance of human rights as set out in paragraph 1. that is why i voted for the agreement.
in writing. − the trade agreement between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and colombia and peru, of the other part (hereinafter referred to as 'the agreement') forms part of the long-standing relationship between the eu and the andean community. the agreement was signed on 26 june 2012 with colombia and peru. the other countries of the andean community may accede by virtue of the accession clause provided for in article 329. in terms of scope and objectives, the agreement is consistent with the eu's free trade policy as expressed in the 2006 global europe strategy and reaffirmed in the 2010 trade, growth and world affairs communication. the convention is comprehensive in that, after a transitional period, virtually all customs duties are abolished and the service obligations go far beyond the gats. the liberalization of services markets is also taking place. i think this is quite critical, because it could seriously damage the local economy, which is why i abstained.
in writing. the commission's aim is to eliminate high tariffs, to remove technical barriers to trade (exporters are to benefit from tariff advantages of eur 270 million per year), to liberalise the markets for services, to protect valuable geographical indications, etc. the inclusion of the human rights clause in article 1 is also positive. however, exporters from these countries already have non-traditional goods such as asparagus, avocados or palm oil on their list. the question arises as to whether it is worthwhile importing colombian or peruvian asparagus into austria. peru is already planning to plant thousands of hectares of new palm oil plantations, which could cause significant damage to tropical forests, water quality and biodiversity, benefit only transnational corporations (again not the small farmer) and displace european dairy products. that is why i abstained.
in writing. - i voted against the european union's free trade agreement with colombia and peru, despite the safeguard clauses negotiated for the first time by the european parliament in a free trade agreement. the european parliament has achieved a great deal in getting colombia and peru to change the law and has also secured the right to observe the reforms. however, i believe that the timing of the signing is still too early. colombia and peru have taken measures, including legislation, to protect the situation of trade unionists, human rights and social activists, but it will probably take a few years to see whether this right is being implemented. the law and reality are still divided. i think the eu should first check whether the projects are actually being implemented and then decide whether the two andean countries are ready to sign the free trade agreement. the murder rate of trade unionists and human rights activists has remained unchanged and has been rising since 2010. by september this year, 235 attacks on human rights activists were registered, including 37 murders. with 35 trade unionists murdered in 2011, colombia remains the most dangerous country in the world for people to organise themselves in a trade union. as a trade unionist, i cannot agree to a free trade agreement unless i see changes.
in writing. − while the european parliament has achieved a lot of positive things in terms of protecting people involved in fundamental rights and trade union activities in colombia and peru, it has also made a lot of progress in the area of human rights. in my view, however, the implementation of the promised reforms in these countries should be monitored first. colombia is still one of the most dangerous countries for people to be in a trade union. in 2011, 35 trade unionists were murdered and hundreds of attacks on human rights activists were registered this year alone. only when the states have demonstrated, through serious efforts and reforms, that they are protecting the fundamental and human rights of their citizens, can a free trade agreement be agreed. that is why i did not agree to the eu-colombia/peru trade agreement.
in writing. - although women age considerably more than men, their hormonal constitution and comparatively lower muscle mass usually make them more frail and needy when they reach advanced age. these gender differences should be taken into account, particularly in the prevention of age-related diseases. this is all the more so as the risk of multiple diseases increases with age and thus the length of hospital stays increases. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat the spread of the disease. rather, the environment needs to be designed to reduce stress factors that play a role in a number of age-related diseases in the long term, such as the double burden of work-life balance or the 'sandwich burden' of caring for children and frail parents at the same time. another starting point is surely the beauty mania that leads to radical starvation cures in teenagers with long-term health consequences into old age. i have taken these points into account in my voting behaviour.
in writing. − ‘ageing’ is a biological, social construct and fact which affects indeed both genders. however, research shows that the incidence of debilitating diseases is much higher in the case of women than among men. even if women have longer life expectancies, during a life time they are – due to biological structure – exposed to more and diverse diseases than men. ‘ageing’ is a complex process that needs to be approached from different aspects: personal (behavioural and physical), social and economic. i believe that ‘ageing’ is still a ‘continuous need of dependence’ and that is why healthcare and social services have to be accessible even for old people facing a more difficult financial situation. we need to improve health and quality of life by implementing policies, programmes and practices that will maintain the ageing population active and healthy. above all, i truly believe that older women need special attention (not only in europe but all over the world). i voted in favour.

in writing. − the introduction of a common financial transaction tax system reflects a harmonised european financial market. this will speed up trade, promote the single market and prevent distortions of competition between different economic players. this will, on the contrary, make the european financial market work efficiently (additional and unnecessary financial transactions could be prevented or excluded). the common financial transaction tax can be considered as a 'financial anchor'. all eu member states and third countries should take advantage of this 'civil' opportunity to introduce a financial instrument that could help europe in its fight against the crisis by generating income.

the beginning. it is not that i am more critical but that the developments in russia have been going in the wrong direction. perhaps it is a good sign, and good symbolically, that we discussed this today when the sakharov prize was handed over and during the human rights discussion, because human rights issues are the most delicate issues concerning russia. the development of democracy is not going in the right direction; it is going in the wrong direction. if we look at the elections they had, there were many irregularities, faults and mistakes at least. many speak of the elections not being free and fair in russia, which i find deplorable. everybody says that putin would have won anyway. so if he was going to win anyway, why then did he not allow real free and fair elections? ngo laws are impeding many ngos from being active. if ngos get money from foreign countries then they are agents of foreign interests, as if democracy and civil liberties were a foreign, and not a russian interest. therefore many russian institutions are not very keen to support some of these ngos in order not to be in touch with ngos which are agents of foreign interest. regarding the pussy riot case, we may not agree with pussy riot’s activities, but the way in which it was handled showed that the justice system is not fair. regarding the recent magnitsky report, i fully endorse what the united states congress decided on in this case. i was able to speak with senator cardin who was very active on this issue years ago, and i have supported him, because it is not acceptable that people who are involved in criminal activities are able to benefit from decisions made by the european union, for example on the visa issue. i think these are many elements where we see negative developments. the ban on homosexual propaganda, as it is called, which now exists in some regions and is being proposed as a federal law, is again a violation of human rights issues. it is unbelievable that, step by step, again and again, russian legislative activities are heading in that direction. we are now having a human rights dialogue but, let us be honest, it is not very effective because very often the ministries concerned – the ministries of the interior and justice – are not part of the human rights dialogue, and then russia starts to criticise the european union for deficiencies. yes they should do this, but the difference is that, although we criticise russia, we also criticise our internal deficiencies. if russia did the same, they could criticise us, but then they should also criticise development in russia itself. of course, syria is the case where disrespect for human rights is most visible. unfortunately, no cooperation has been possible up to now. we can say that trade is another issue on which we can cooperate. that is all very well, but as commissioner de gucht said very recently, there are big problems. russia joined, but then they decided on several laws that were not in compliance with what is necessary under wto rules. so it is very hard to have a very pragmatic approach. nevertheless, i think we should try to find cooperation with russia where it is possible. i am also absolutely in favour of visa liberalisation, because this is not for the functionaries but it is especially for the citizens. therefore, to end my short speech, let us be pragmatic but at the same time strict on human rights and on the violation of the wto, because partnership can only be an honest partnership and not a dishonest one. if we want to be honest we have to fight for human rights everywhere, including in russia.

the commission has already made a number of proposals. the crucial question for us, when we assess the elections of 28 october, is whether we are dealing with a parliament that actually reflects the will of the ukrainian people or not. and i think that, despite all the shortcomings that we may have noted - how we assess them is another matter - we can say that, in principle, this parliament is in line with the will of the ukrainian people. not even the most vocal critics of this election will be able to prove otherwise. all the exit polls also predicted the election outcome pretty accurately, and then they found it. that means that we are dealing with a parliament that is based on legitimacy and legality. the five constituencies where irregularities were found will also have their own by-elections, which will also be monitored internationally. we must also recognise that ukraine has a will to modernise - driven not only by the population but also by the government - that ukrainians have a will to improve the rule of law, particularly in the area of criminal procedure, and that they are making serious efforts to fight corruption. and they are even further along and more committed than some eu countries! i wish i had said that clearly to the balkans! it is therefore sensible and in the interests of europe to push this association agreement forward and not to put undue pressure on ukraine, because it is not helping anyone there. and if you keep bringing up the name of tymoshenko, whenever you talk to ukrainians, you will find that they have very different concerns from mrs tymoshenko. we should have our interest in the association agreement and the development of ukraine as a democratic country in mind!
i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. the work of the fundamental rights agency should be unquestioned. without them, it would be difficult to evaluate the rights enshrined in the charter and other binding documents. it also has the function of continually calling attention to and respecting fundamental rights. human rights are indivisible and universal. the people of europe need to be assured that they can rely on it in all member states and in all situations of life, without prejudice to their individual characteristics. the multiannual framework for the fundamental rights agency is therefore welcome in principle, because it is necessary. it is indeed surprising that the council has not followed the commission's proposal to include judicial cooperation in criminal matters in the area of the agency, as would be the case under the lisbon treaty. the council considers that criminal matters are explicitly excluded from the scope of its activities. this leaves the agency without the possibility of bringing its own prosecutions in such important areas as the respect of human rights in criminal prosecutions, in court proceedings and in the execution of sentences. respect for human rights must be applied to all law enforcement authorities, including the police and the judiciary, and in particular the protection of personal data must be guaranteed in this context. the protection of personal data is one of the fundamental rights issues of the 21st century.
i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. the european monitoring centre on racism and xenophobia was already an agency for fundamental rights when it was established. the council of europe and the osce are also responsible for human rights. it is certainly incomprehensible to the taxpayer today that the special representative for human rights and the council of europe commissioner for human rights, for example, appointed in the summer of 2012, are supposed to do exactly the same job. this duplicity makes it difficult for taxpayers to understand, at a time when austerity packages are being hammered across europe, why the fundamental rights agency has a budget of €20 million in 2012 alone, especially since this eu body, contrary to its name, is less concerned with protecting fundamental rights than with politically correct spying on critical citizens and lobbying for third world immigrants and obscure marginalised groups. i therefore believe that it is high time that not only the subsidy jungle of the european union but also that of the various eu agencies be explored. this includes in particular the eu agency for fundamental rights, which should be reviewed for its usefulness. the eu's ever-growing financial needs, which are being created by the assumption of new responsibilities and the creation of questionable eu institutions, must finally be curbed, especially in times of crisis.
i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. madam vice-president, you said that the work of the human rights agency was in danger because the council did not adopt the work programme in time. i believe that the work of the agency is rather endangered by the fact that there are serious shortcomings in the management of this agency. i would just point out that in connection with the discharge decision the european parliament has strongly urged the agency to improve the planning of budget implementation after there was a transfer of almost 7 million and there were extremely serious problems in the recruitment procedures. only 59 of the 72 posts needed could be filled. the budgetary development of this agency is of particular interest, as is the development of the staff of the agency over the years. the budget has increased by 117% in 4 years to 20 million at present, by over 17% from 2009 to 2010 alone. i think it is particularly dramatic that of this budget of 20 million, two thirds is spent on administrative expenditure and only one third is used for operational tasks. and if you look at the human resources development, the staff in this agency has tripled in four years. i therefore urge the commission - and i also recommend it - to examine the agency closely for efficiency, to examine the budget, the budgetary management and also to control the personnel management before any further decisions are taken on the annual planning and the budget.

in writing. − the scope of the so-called fundamental rights agency should not be extended, but rather this eu body should be closed. finally, the council of europe and the osce are also responsible for the protection of human rights. the commission has also proposed that the commission should be given the task of drawing up a report on the implementation of the fundamental rights directive. the fundamental rights agency, contrary to its name, has very little to do with the protection of fundamental rights. the main task of this body is the politically correct spying on citizens who express their legitimate dissatisfaction with the unrestricted mass immigration to europe. and another area of activity of the supposed defenders of fundamental rights is lobbying for marginalized groups such as homosexuals. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the commission is proposing to relax asylum and immigration laws. because this is clearly contrary to the interests of the european peoples, there is another reason for the rapid closure of the eu agency for fundamental rights. i therefore voted against the report.
in writing. − the tightening of the written declaration guidelines is unfounded, unnecessary and further demonstrates the eu establishment's desire to suppress initiatives from individual meps or a small group. it is not otherwise that the very issue of the written declarations, which was also taken up by many citizens of the union and for whose support there was always a massive campaign on the spot or by e-mail, is now almost impossible to explain. whereas previously it was possible for each member to put a subject he considered particularly important to the fore by means of a written statement, now at least ten members from three political groups are required. this is in complete contradiction to the original purpose of the instrument, which was precisely to promote individual activities. the groups have every opportunity. all the alibis, such as the european citizens' initiative or the recent fuss about the nobel prize for the eu, which is intended to make citizens feel that they have a say, cannot hide the true approach of the eurocrats, who try to do everything in the smallest possible circle behind closed doors. i therefore naturally voted against this undemocratic approach.

in writing. − the recent conviction of russia by the european court of human rights for torture and the recent raids on opposition figures once again demonstrate russia's need to catch up on human rights and democracy. this is hardly surprising, given the 70 years of communist past that are yet to be worked out. the west, which likes to play the guardian of democracy and human rights, is not without its faults. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. and here too, freedom of expression is constantly under threat and pressure is exerted on the media. the eu should not presume to be the world's leading authority on these issues, especially when negotiating with moscow. that is why i have rejected this report.
in writing. − israel has responded to the recent un general assembly resolution on the upgrading of the status of the palestinians by announcing that it will build 3,000 more homes in east jerusalem and the west bank. the planned construction in area e1 would extend deep into palestinian territory and de facto divide it into northern and southern parts. the plans are particularly delicate because the palestinians fear being cut off from east jerusalem, which they want to make their capital in a bid for a two-state solution. the creation of a viable, coherent and sovereign palestinian state is also at risk. the joint resolution, which was co-sponsored by all parliament's political groups, calls, inter alia, for the israeli government's decision to withhold usd 100 million of palestinian tax revenues at the expense of the palestinian authority budget to be repealed, and for the eu and its member states to fully and effectively implement the existing eu legislation and the existing bilateral treaties between the eu and israel. i voted in favour of the resolution because i believe that it is very balanced and takes account of the interests of both the israelis and the palestinians.

in writing. the steel industry is in a veritable crisis, as the figures show. demand is falling sharply, which has a dramatic effect on the steel labour market figures. in 1970, there were one million people employed in the steel industry in the eu, but today there are only 369 000. this has a further impact on the workforce in downstream industries. it is also clear that more and more cheap steel is being imported into europe from countries such as russia, china and turkey. in hardly any other region in the world are the environmental constraints on steel production as high as in the eu, making it increasingly difficult for companies to compete in the global market. i voted in favour of the resolution because i share the view that the eu must pay greater attention to industrial policy. this is the only way to ensure the long-term competitiveness of european industry on the world market.
in writing. the steel industry was the backbone of european industrial society for over a century. the prosperity of entire regions depended on the prosperity of this sector. i represent a constituency in the region around linz in upper austria where, contrary to the general trend, this sector has been expanded and developed. this link can be seen in its effects on the economy and employment. it is not for me to speculate on why the steel sector has increasingly moved away from europe over the last two decades. the fact is, however, that the deindustrialisation of europe has had serious consequences for the competitiveness of some member states and has impaired their macroeconomic controls. it is necessary to consider whether it is really sensible to neglect the industrial production sector in the course of the progressive globalization. the priority must be to modernise this sector in a sustainable way. the current crisis teaches us that we need more real economy and a turn to the manufacturing sector. the reindustrialisation of europe would undoubtedly improve the competitiveness of the continent. the steel industry has a key role to play in this. the commission's decision to adopt a european steel action plan is therefore to be welcomed. it is important to implement the necessary measures quickly and without delay, taking account in particular of the economic, regional and social implications.
